A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Moner and retain matching methods, datasets, and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the new 3D material in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original fastMRI and MoDL reconstruction experiments, motion-estimation results, runtime comparisons, and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds simulated 3D reconstruction experiments and a real-acquisition study involving two scans of one subject.

M1.justification: The original 2D method is retained, but Appendix A.1 adds an implemented 3D extension. It uses stack-of-radial data, a 2D inverse Fourier transform, 3D back-projection, and six rigid-motion parameters per motion state. V1 discusses 3D extension only as future work.

E1.justification: V2 adds simulated motion on a 240×240×240 brain volume and actual motion-corrupted and motion-free T1w 3D acquisitions from one subject. This extends the original simulated 2D fastMRI/MoDL evaluation to volumetric reconstruction and real acquisition conditions.

E2.justification: The corresponding 2D comparisons retain NuIFFT, TV, DRN-DCMB, and Score-MoCo, with TV and Score-MoCo retained for motion estimation. The new 3D experiments reuse NuIFFT; no new comparator algorithm or substantive baseline modification is documented.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces 3D simulation protocols with 120 motion states, acceleration factors 2×/4×, and motion ranges ±5/±10. The acquired-data protocol uses 650 estimated motion stages, three instructed head movements, and a separate motion-free reference. Previously stated 2D splits and optimization budgets remain unchanged; newly disclosed 2D preprocessing details do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The three existing component ablations retain their settings and aggregate results. V2 adds focused 3D motion-recovery case analyses: Figure 11 compares estimated trajectories with simulated ground truth, while Figure 13 examines consistency with the real subject's instructed movements. These provide limited additional diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V1 reports ± values for component ablations but lacks statistical tests and uncertainty for the main image-quality comparisons. V2 adds mean±STD reporting for PSNR and SSIM in Tables 2 and 7 and t-test significance categories throughout Tables 1–7. Neither version specifies seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds 3D quantitative and acquired-data results. For example, Table 6 reports PSNR/SSIM of 31.58/0.844 for Moner versus 23.64/0.499 for NuIFFT at AF=2×, MR=±5. Existing 2D Moner means remain unchanged, but Score-MoCo's MoDL AF=2×, MR=±15 result changes from 32.49/0.762 to 33.90/0.795. Newly reported tests mark fastMRI PSNR differences between Moner and Score-MoCo as nonsignificant.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds the formal 3D rotation matrix and translation vector in Equation 10 and the corresponding volumetric projection relationship. The existing Fourier-slice derivation, 2D method equations, and motion-error definitions remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-data-free joint reconstruction and motion estimation, projection-based optimization, and coarse-to-fine hash encoding. Claims of comparable in-domain performance and superior out-of-domain performance remain substantively unchanged; the 3D appendix expands evidence and capabilities without rewriting these main claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies intra-acquisition motion, non-rigid motion, and spin-history effects as limitations and discusses deformation-field modeling as a possible extension. It characterizes the acquired-data validation as preliminary. Appendix A.2 also corrects the motion-error interpretation from higher-is-better to lower-is-better without changing its formula.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies image contrasts, orientations, spacing, golden-angle sampling, spoke length, view counts, and 18 motion stages. It also discloses the MLP width and activation choices. Appendix A.1 supplies scanner, sequence, volume, and motion-state details for the new studies. These substantially expand reproducibility information; existing baseline implementation links remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Catalán et al. (2023) and distinguishes its Fourier-slice neural-field approach from Moner. It also acknowledges that some earlier INR methods address dynamic range through relative L2 losses, replacing the blanket omission claim, and cites Reed et al. (2021) for possible non-rigid extensions.

P1.justification: V2 selectively edits the abstract and introductory discussion, separates datasets from preprocessing in Section 4.1, removes the brief reproducibility statement, and inserts the 3D appendix section. Author information is reformatted. Most method and results prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the 3D schematic, reconstruction and trajectory figures, and Table 6. It splits the original combined PSNR/SSIM table into Tables 2 and 7, adds statistical annotations, replaces Figure 4 examples with annotated detail views, and labels the encoding-ablation trajectory by motion stages. Original appendix image grids are retained as Figures 15–18 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's restriction to simulated 2D validation by documenting and testing a 3D extension, including actual motion-corrupted acquisitions. The added sampling and implementation details close important reproducibility gaps, while uncertainty and significance reporting make comparisons more assessable. The gains are tempered by the single-subject real study, NuIFFT-only 3D comparisons, and unexplained revisions to some Score-MoCo scores, but materially strengthen the paper's practical evidence and transparency.
